plain_result: Option names affected this open Laya model on a selected panel. The registered prediction that other contextual positions would carry more of the name-binding contrast than option-marker positions was not supported. This does not establish a new mechanism or a reliable controller.

model.name: Laya
model.scope: A separate open typed-decision model. These local tests did not run TypeSafe Jev or Cloudflare Clef.
model.runtime: Pinned CPU FP32, four threads, SDPA; attention fast path disabled consistently for observed and unobserved calls.

initial_tool_check.scope: Eight related invented tool-selection inputs, each run twice. Tools had different actual behavior and supplied feedback. This is not a population accuracy estimate; the failed requirement remains closed.

name_binding_panel.selection: Fixed hash selection, balanced by the synthetic reference class within each workflow; no model-score selection.
name_binding_panel.question_change: Explicit binary question definitions and original state strings were retained, while the question type was converted to a two-option choice. This is not unchanged original-API benchmark accuracy.
name_binding_panel.reference: Synthetic teacher labels and probabilities; not independently verified ground truth.
name_binding_panel.clear_conflict_definition: All six aligned/neutral binding-by-order decisions agree with the reference, while reversed polar names produce a unique opposite decision in both orders. Both reference classes occur.

boundary_test.method: At the encoder-to-head boundary, replace the two option-marker rows, the other rows, or both, using the corresponding aligned-name input as donor for the reversed-name input. Run the original two-layer decision head and scorer. Facts and option definitions are the same between donor and recipient.
boundary_test.registered_hypothesis: Context dominance: G > 0 and T = (context-only margin - marker-only margin) - 0.25*G > 0, pooled and in each workflow/order, with the state-clustered bootstrap lower bound for pooled T above zero. G is the full-donor minus full-recipient reference-logit margin.
boundary_test.interval_unit: State, with both orders averaged before workflow-stratified resampling; two fixed confirmation workflows, 2,000 draws.
boundary_test.interpretation: Descriptively, marker-state swaps carried most average name-binding contrast on this panel. This opposite-direction observation is not a replacement primary success. Marker states are contextualized and have a direct residual path to the marker-only final scorer; other positions act through attention. Near-zero complement-swap effect does not establish ignored context, a name-specific circuit, or a deployable repair.

checks.terminal_log_note: The audit hashed its empty stdout log before appending its terminal status JSON. The terminal review reconciles this one operational-log change; scientific records and source hashes did not change.

operational_history.first_name_conflict_attempt: Stopped before the first model forward because a logging argument name collided. No model outcome was available. Original STOP and sources remain unchanged.
operational_history.separate_v2: A disclosed operational amendment changed the logging parameter and output context, while preserving selected states, model, inputs, methods and scientific rules. This is not an independent scientific replication.

limits: Reference agreement was weaker in the other workflows; invoice behavior is not a universal direction of bias.
The checkpoint was studied on official test states without proof that these states were unseen during its training.
Bindings, orders and head interventions reuse the same 32 states; they are not 384 independent cases.
This tests one model and a particular computational boundary, not heterogeneous organ coordination, new-rule transfer or planning.
No failed test was reclassified as a success, and no new mechanism or broadly reliable fix is established.
next_step: A heterogeneous controller remains a proposal. It needs modules with distinct useful abilities, observable feedback, and comparisons with fixed selection, simple rules, random selection and all-module execution at matched cost. A separate design would be required before another study.
transformation: Selected completed aggregate counts, fixed comparisons, operational history and reviewed limits. No raw hidden states, per-case scores, model weights, process identifiers, credentials or absolute local paths copied. Earlier public evidence records remain unchanged.
